lede: Lodi celebrates with a downtown Parade of Lights that draws nearly 30,000 people and a Festival of Trees at the San Joaquin County Museum.
celebrates: Lodi kicks off the holidays with the Parade of Lights in downtown on Thursday, December 3, 2026, hosted by Kiwanis of Greater Lodi, with Santa arriving on a Lodi fire truck. The San Joaquin County Historical Museum at Micke Grove holds its 34th Annual Festival of Trees the first weekend of December, and Hutchins Street Square lists The Nutcracker on December 12 on the City of Lodi calendar.
lastyear: Lodi's Parade of Lights ran on Thursday, December 4, 2025, according to Visit Stockton and local posts. Visit Lodi says the parade draws nearly 30,000 spectators each year, and the evening ends with Santa on a fire truck.
facts: Visit Lodi describes the Parade of Lights as a tradition that transforms downtown Lodi into a winter wonderland of lights, music and community cheer. The Festival of Trees at the San Joaquin County Museum is a long running tradition with 60 uniquely decorated trees, children's activities and make and take crafts, and 2026 is its 34th year.
trains: Lodi does not run a Santa train of its own. Families looking for a Christmas train ride can check the Stockton page and the Sacramento guide for rides in the region, including River Fox Train's Magical Christmas Train in West Sacramento.

faq: When is the Lodi Parade of Lights in 2026?
Thursday, December 3, 2026. The parade begins at 6:17 pm in downtown Lodi and is free, according to Visit Lodi.
Where can kids see Santa in Lodi?
Santa arrives on a Lodi fire truck at the end of the Parade of Lights on December 3.
What is the Festival of Trees in Lodi?

The 34th Annual Festival of Trees at the San Joaquin County Museum at Micke Grove has decorated Christmas trees, children's activities and crafts. See the live listing on our site for the dates and prices.
Is the Lodi Christmas parade free?
Yes. Visit Lodi lists the Parade of Lights as a free, family friendly event.
